newsitem.title: USA: Late NYMEX Hub natgas still down slightly.
newsitem.headline: Late NYMEX Hub natgas still down slightly.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures remained down slightly late Tuesday in moderate activity, with light technical selling still pressuring the complex after an early rally attempt stalled, sources said.
At 1440 EDT, May was still down 1.1 cents at $1.935 per million British thermal units, while June was 2.4 cents lower at $1.985. Most other months were a half to 2.5 cents lower.

"The screen tried to rally and then fell off. When they couldn't get it up, the natural reaction was to sell it," said one trader, adding 6-10 day forecasts were supportive but moderate temps later in the month could mean some pressure.
While favorable spreads and bullish weather forecasts encouraged some buying, few saw much upside, with more moderate spring weather likely later in the month.
Forecasters were calling for below-normal Midwest and eastern weather through mid-month.
Technical traders agreed the spot contract needed to settle above $2 and then $2.10 to trigger a rally. Otherwise, they said prices were stuck in a range, with support still pegged at $1.825-1.85.
Early estimates for Wednesday's weekly AGA gas stock report ranged from a draw of 10 bcf to a build of 30 bcf. For the same week last year, stocks fell by 15 bcf.

Colder Midwest and eastern weather forecasts firmed the physical market Tuesday. Gulf Coast prices climbed a couple of cents to the $1.95-2.00 area. Midcontinent pipes were up a similar amount to $1.85-1.90. Gas at New York city gate again jumped more than 10 cents to the mid-to-high $2.30s on the approaching cold.
NYMEX said 20,192 Hub contracts traded at 1350 EDT.
As of 1440 EDT, no Permian or Alberta natgas futures were traded.
On KCBT, May stayed down 1.5 cents at $1.78, while deferreds remained mixed. The East/West spread widened by 0.4 cent to 15.5 cents (NYMEX premium).
Physical prices at Waha gained three cents Tuesday to the $1.85-1.90 area.
